description.content: State of the nearest ancestor tabset (returned by useParentTabsetState).
The user most recently interacted with this tabset (by pointer or focus).
The tabset is collapsed to just its header.

While a separator is being dragged, this reflects how the tabset is shown (e.g. collapsed as soon as it reaches its collapsed size), which the model (and useParentTabset().isCollapsed()) only reflects once the drag ends.
A tabset that's collapsed to fit (see isCollapsedToFit) is collapsed, although the model has it expanded.
A maximized tabset is shown expanded, but it's still collapsed when it is restored.

The tabset is collapsed only because it doesn't fit (e.g. the workspace is narrower than its tabsets' minimum sizes; see TabsetNode.collapsible). The model has it expanded, and it's shown expanded again once it fits.
It can't be expanded until then (e.g. useParentTabset().expand() does nothing), so a toolbar can hide (or disable) its "expand" button.

The tabset can be collapsed (or is collapsed, and can be expanded), e.g. to show or hide a toolbar button: it has the collapsible flag, isn't the only tabset in the workspace, and has a sibling that isn't collapsed.

The user cannot drag the tabset as a whole, because:

  • It has the disableDrag flag, or one of its tabs does
  • The Workspace has the disabled prop
  • It's the only tabset in the workspace (see isRoot), and can't be dragged to another workspace (see the Workspace's dragGroup prop; tabsets with the keepWhenEmpty flag can't be)
  • A tabset is maximized
The tabset is the root of the model, so it's the only tabset in the workspace.
Some controls aren't useful for the only tabset (e.g. maximizing it), so this can be used to hide them.
